open_points.subject: A08 rule 4 (idempotency key checks for read operations)
open_points.text: "...otherwise the text split on `+` ... must be a list of distinct plain field names..." and later "For a `read` operation the key is not used and not checked"
open_points.question: When proposing/accepting a binding for a `read` operation, must malformed `idempotency_key` text be refused, or ignored entirely?
options: Validate `idempotency_key` syntax for all operations, including `read`
open_points.default_guess: Skip validation for `read` operations and ignore malformed key declarations there.

open_points.subject: A16/A20 request size ceiling enforcement
open_points.text: A16: "its size is within `surface_request_bytes_max`"; A20: "A request one byte over `surface_request_bytes_max` is refused"
open_points.question: What exact byte representation is measured for request size (raw transport bytes, decoded JSON bytes, canonical re-encoding, or MCP frame payload)?
options: Measure raw incoming payload bytes before parsing
Measure UTF-8 bytes of decoded request JSON text
open_points.default_guess: Measure raw incoming MCP payload bytes before parsing.

open_points.subject: A16 rule 6 continuation token
open_points.text: "...a continuation token that is malformed or names no position of that list is refused. ... The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned"
open_points.question: What is the token’s concrete encoding/shape and validation rule, so different implementations produce/accept the same token?
options: Plain integer store position as string
Opaque signed/encoded blob containing store position
Structured object with list identity + position
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque token that decodes to a single store position integer and reject decode failures.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 1 and A17 rule 1 header-name collision
open_points.text: "...installation whose credential header has the name of a required header refuses to start"
open_points.question: Is header-name comparison case-sensitive or case-insensitive (HTTP header names are case-insensitive), and how are duplicate required headers handled?
options: Compare case-insensitively and refuse any collision/duplicate after normalization
Normalize to lowercase on read and deduplicate by first/last wins
open_points.default_guess: Compare case-insensitively after lowercase normalization and refuse on any collision or duplicate.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped-node element processing after an element failure
open_points.text: "A mapped node, once selected, runs every element it can in list order..." and "any failed element makes it failed for its dependants"
open_points.question: If one element fails (not waits), must the node continue executing later elements in that same advance step, or stop immediately?
options: Continue remaining elements in order, then mark mapped node failed
Stop at first failed element and leave later elements unattempted
open_points.default_guess: Continue all elements in order and then treat the mapped node as failed for dependants.
